text: The picture arrived before the person did. Your Neptune sits on their Sun. Their whole effort at being somebody definite arrives inside your imagination, and your imagination is not a neutral surface. You did not decide to do this. By the time you noticed you held a view of them, it was already a generous one, and already somewhat larger than anything they had actually done in front of you. What that gives them is worth saying before the rest. Most people are met at their current size. You meet them at the size they reach on a good day, and you describe it back to them in words they would be embarrassed to use about themselves. They are rarely embarrassed to hear it. If they are building something that has no proof yet, your belief works like early funding: it arrives when nothing else would justify it. People do get taller in that kind of attention, and this is not an illusion you should be talked out of entirely. The bill comes later, and they pay most of it. Steady admiration is pleasant for a while and expensive after that. They cannot bring you a plain failure, because the failure has to be fitted into a story where they are remarkable, and the fitting costs them more effort than the failure did. The small confessions stop first. Then the unflattering ones. After a few years you may be handed a carefully kept version of a person and take it for closeness. They often cannot say what is wrong. They only know they feel watched by something kind, and that being kindly watched is not the same as being known. Your own side of the ledger is not clean. Once your imagination settles on someone, you stop gathering information about them, and you will defend the picture against the evidence far longer than you would for anybody else. You extend doubts the benefit you should have kept. You forgive early, which looks like generosity and is sometimes a way of not looking. Your outline goes soft as well. Around them you can turn into an audience rather than a person with wants, and nobody ever asks the audience what it needs. The correction comes whether you invite it or not. One day they do something ordinary and irritating while you are tired, and the picture slips, and the drop tends to be steeper than the offense deserves. That fall is not a betrayal on their part. It is the price of the height, arriving on time. Working with this is duller than the feeling it produces. Ask them factual questions and listen to the answers as answers. Let them be boring in your company without rescuing the moment. When you catch yourself describing them to somebody else, check how much of the description you could actually source. You lose an image you were maintaining largely on your own. In exchange you get someone who can be tired in front of you, and being tired in front of somebody is a different thing from being admired by them.

Some contacts take you somewhere. This one holds a door open and waits. Your Neptune makes an easy angle to their Sun, so your imagination has a clean route to their sense of who they are, and absolutely nothing obliges either of you to use it. When somebody does reach for it, here is what happens. They tell you what they are trying to do with some part of their life. You hear the version that has not happened yet, and you say that version out loud, without decorating it or promising it. Most people answer an ambition with a cost estimate. You answer with a shape. That is scarce, and it lands hardest on a plan too young to be defended, which is exactly when most plans die. Skipped, it produces no symptom whatsoever. You can know this person for a decade, enjoy them, describe them warmly to other people, and never once look closely enough to be surprised. Sextiles do not complain when they are ignored. There is no crisis that forces the issue, only a mild sense years later that you were fond of somebody you never quite got to. The cost to them is small here and still worth naming. A generous reading is a reading. Someone who is regularly spoken to in terms a little better than their conduct starts to notice the gap, and the noticing is private. They may decide there is no point telling you about a day when they were petty or careless, since it does not belong in the account you seem to be keeping. Nothing dramatic follows. The relationship simply gets a floor under it that they are careful not to fall through. Your part of the cost is inattention dressed as goodwill. Because this angle never chafes, you are not forced to update. It is easy to keep an approximate idea of someone for years when the approximate idea is flattering and no evidence ever contradicts it loudly. Their Sun would not mind being asked a hard question. You are the one who avoids it, on the grounds that the mood is good. What switches this on is deliberate use, and the useful moves are unheroic. Ask what they want that they have stopped saying out loud. Offer your read of their situation as a read rather than a compliment. Be present for something of theirs that could fail. Spent on purpose, this turns into the friendship where they can think about their own life more ambitiously than they manage alone, and where your imagination gets a real subject instead of a pleasant one.

Something in you keeps rewriting them while they are still talking. Your Neptune squares their Sun, so your habit of seeing past the surface runs at an angle to their business of presenting a definite self. They say plainly what they want. You hear a subtler motive, a finer aim, or an old wound behind it, and the thing they actually said goes by unrecorded. Your revisions run in two directions and they alternate. Some days the person in front of you is finer than anything the record shows, and you supply the nobility yourself. Other days they are more damaged than they have ever claimed, and you supply that too. Both readings walk straight past the person, who is neither, and who has usually described their position accurately and in short words. Here is what that does to them. They keep asserting themselves and keep meeting a soft correction. Say the ambition out loud and it gets translated into something less vulgar. Admit the ordinary motive, money or credit or wanting to win, and watch it get upgraded into a better one on your face. Being upgraded is a strange kind of contradiction. There is nothing to argue with, so they end up either accepting a self they did not claim or insisting on the crude version until they sound defensive. Around you their directness can start to feel like bad manners, and that is an expensive thing for a Sun to learn. Your side of the friction is real too. Their plainness can feel like a shutter coming down on a room you were enjoying. When they state a limit or a preference flatly, you may experience it as coarseness, or as proof that they are smaller than you hoped, and disappointment can settle into a standing mood rather than a response to anything. Watch for the version where you become quietly sad about them as a permanent condition. That mood costs nothing and reports nothing. What the square is good for is accuracy at the point where you least want it. This person will not sit still for a portrait. They keep moving and keep insisting on their own account, and if you stay in the room you will eventually have to take that account seriously, which is a discipline your imagination gets nowhere else. Their edges do the same work for you that a frame does for a photograph. Meanwhile you are the one asking them, without ever asking it directly, whether the self they present is the whole of them. That question is worth being asked by somebody. Hard angles do not settle. Over a long acquaintance this one turns into a working habit: you check the sentence you think you heard, they learn that the poetic reading is not always wrong, and the two of you get further than either would with someone easier.

They looked luminous to you early, and nothing since has managed to disturb it. Your Neptune trines their Sun, so your imagination flows toward whoever they are with no resistance anywhere along the way. You have never had to work at thinking well of them. On the days they are being difficult, the charitable reading arrives first and arrives on its own. As an experience this is lovely and mostly harmless. You are their best audience. What they are aiming at makes immediate sense to you, including the parts they cannot justify, and there are few things a person needs more than one listener who does not require the justification. For anything they make, perform, or build, you are unusually useful company: your sympathy reaches the intention behind the work and not only the version that came out. The problem with an admirer who never fails is that they stop being an instrument. If your reaction is warm regardless of what they do, then your warmth carries no information, and some part of them knows it. They cannot find out from you how they are landing. Praise from you is free, so it does not count, and eventually they take the question of whether the thing was any good to somebody harsher. That is a real loss for both of you and it happens without a word being said. There is a further habit worth watching in yourself. Because your picture of them is comfortable, you may quietly attach your own unlived life to it. Their projects become the ones you follow; their success feels like something happening to you; your imagination gets its exercise through their biography rather than your own. Trines make that easy and never charge for it up front. You may also find that you excuse conduct you would not excuse in anyone else, not by deciding to, but because the unflattering interpretation simply never occurs to you. The repair is not to become critical. It is to become specific. Tell them which part worked and which part did not, in ordinary language, and let them see that your regard survives you having an opinion. Ask what they are actually worried about instead of assuring them it will be fine. Keep one project of your own that they have nothing to do with. Handled that way, this stays what it already is at its best: a person who can stand in front of you without armor, and an imagination of yours that has somewhere generous to go, without either of you mistaking the ease for the whole relationship.

Longing works better at a distance, and this contact supplies the distance built in. Your Neptune stands opposite their Sun. Across that gap they stop being a set of ordinary facts and become a figure: the bright one, the capable one, the one who seems to have arrived somewhere you have not. You are not inventing them out of nothing. You are looking at a real light through your own weather and filling in the rest. Casting is the main event here. The role you hand them changes with your own state, and it changes fast. On a steady week they are impressive. On a thin week they are the person who has what you were denied, and the same behavior reads as arrogance. Neither reading is reporting on them. Both are reporting on the distance, and the distance is the aspect. Consider what it is like to be on the other end. They are carrying a wish that is not theirs. Someone across the room has decided they are solid, so they now have to keep being solid, including on the days they are not. Your admiration puts a floor under their conduct and a ceiling over their honesty. Many people in that position quietly stop mentioning their doubts to the person who most needs them to be certain, and then wonder why the closeness has a hollow spot in it. If they ever do come apart in front of you, the shock is yours as much as theirs. What it costs you is a shape of your own. Standing opposite a defined person is a way of not being one. Your side of the axis holds everything that has no edges: the yearning, the imagination, the willingness to leave things open. It is entirely possible to spend years in the company of someone bright and never once say what you want, because wanting anything specific would spoil the arrangement. That is not humility. It is a way of staying safe from a plain answer. An opposition is also a supply line, which is the half people forget. They hold definition, the nerve to say this is who I am and take the consequences. You hold the capacity to be moved, to admit that things are unfinished, to let a person be more than their outline. Each of you is short of exactly what the other has too much of, and the trade is available at any point. The way it improves is by getting closer to unremarkable. Spend time with them in circumstances that have no glamour in them at all: errands, illness, a long delay. Watch what they do rather than what they seem to be. Say one specific thing you want from them, out loud, and let the answer be whatever it is. The figure fades a little with each of those, and the person who comes up behind it is someone you can actually be with.

Their moods get into you without a border crossing. Your Neptune has moved in with their Moon. The part of you without edges now lives where they feel, need, and reach for comfort. You pick up their state before they report it. Within an hour of being together the room is running on a weather system neither of you can trace to its owner. For them the first effect is relief, and it is not a small one. They can be unhappy near you without having to explain the unhappiness or perform recovering from it. You do not meet a feeling with a question about what caused it. You meet it with more room. People who have spent their lives managing their moods for other people find this almost startling, and they tend to attach quickly. Then comes the part the tradition rarely puts on the reader's side. Sympathy is not supply. A Moon asks for concrete things: the meal, the lift, the same hour on the same day, the arrangement that holds when nobody feels like holding it. You are inclined to answer all of that with atmosphere. You are moved, you are present, you understand completely, and by Thursday nothing has been organized. From their chair the care is obviously genuine and somehow does not land in the place where the need was. Complaining about it feels ungrateful, so they usually do not, and the shortfall goes into a quiet account neither of you audits. There is a harder thing to look at, and it is the reason this contact deserves a warning that is not about anybody lying. Their need is where your imagination fits best, so you can end up preferring them in need. When they are struggling, you know exactly what to do with them. When they are competent, busy, and fine, you may feel oddly at a loose end, or find yourself gently reminding them of their difficulties. Nobody does this on purpose. It is worth catching anyway, because being loved best at your lowest is a strange arrangement to live inside. What it costs you is the border. You take on grief that is not yours and lose track of your own evening. Your judgment about their situation arrives slower than your feeling about it, so you can be deeply moved by a state of affairs you have not actually assessed. Somebody has to notice the difference between being with them and dissolving into them. It is not going to be the aspect. The useful work here is unglamorous and it does not spoil the tenderness. Turn one feeling a week into an action with a time attached. Ask them what would actually help, and take a plain answer plainly. Notice when their competence disappoints you. Care that includes the arrangements is worth several times the care that only includes the mood.

Gentleness is on the table between you, and nothing whatsoever obliges you to reach for it. Your Neptune makes a workable angle to their Moon: your imagination can meet their feelings without either flooding them or losing itself, which is the difference between this and the heavier Neptune contacts. Nothing here overwhelms anyone. Reached for, though, it has a signature. They can be in a bad state in front of you and you will not try to fix it on a schedule. You have a knack for making a difficult evening feel less like an emergency, mostly by not treating it as one. Shared silence works. So does the sort of company where nobody is required to be interesting. If they have a private life that runs on things they cannot say properly, you are one of the few people who does not need them to say it properly. Their habits are a shore. A person with reliable comforts, regular hours, and a clear sense of what they need is steadying company for someone whose inner life has no fixed outline, and you are more porous than you usually admit. Time around them tends to leave you more located than you were. Because this is a sextile, all of it stays optional. Left alone it produces a mild and pleasant acquaintance: someone you find soothing, whom you see now and then, and who would describe you as easy to be around without being able to say much else. That is a real relationship and a fraction of what is available. No pressure inside the angle will make either of you bother. There is one soft cost, and it belongs mostly to them. Your kindness makes an awkward subject harder to raise, not easier. If the atmosphere between you is always mild, a complaint arrives sounding coarse by comparison, and they may swallow small things for a long time rather than be the one who spoils the tone. You will not see this happening. You will only notice that nothing difficult ever seems to come up. Spending this on purpose looks like asking a direct question while the mood is good rather than waiting for trouble, and letting them see you when you are not being gentle. Used that way it feeds both of you instead of only soothing you, and an honest disagreement becomes something the two of you can have rather than something that spoils the tone.

You are being kind at somebody who wanted something else. A square between your Neptune and their Moon puts your formlessness across the path of their need for a thing that holds. They reach for a specific comfort: an answer, a plan, the reassurance said in words, the arrangement confirmed. You offer understanding, possibility, and your genuine presence. Both are real and they do not exchange at par. The failure is slow and it makes almost no noise. They ask what is happening on Saturday and get a mood in reply. They ask whether you meant the thing you said, and the answer is warm and does not resolve. Nothing you do is unkind, which is exactly what makes it hard for them to name. Complaining about a person who is obviously generous feels petty, so they hold it, and the holding turns into a low background hunger they cannot source. When it finally comes out it sounds much larger than the individual incidents, and you will be honestly bewildered, because from inside your side of this you have been nothing but available. What this costs you is less visible and no lighter. Their need for specifics can arrive on you as a demand to become smaller. Being asked exactly what you will do, and when, and whether you are sure, can feel like being audited by someone who has decided your softness is a defect. Under that pressure the natural move is to go vaguer in self-defense, which produces precisely the fog they were complaining about. You are not being evasive. You are being asked to give a firm answer about something that does not exist in you in firm form yet. There is one more thing to watch, and it is on your side of the ledger. You can idealize their vulnerability. Their moods become material for your imagination, tender and meaningful, and in the process you may stop noticing that the mood is attached to a person with an actual difficulty, one that has a cause and possibly a remedy. Feeling deeply about someone is not the same as looking at their situation. This friction trains something worth having. You learn to convert a feeling into an act with a time on it, which is a skill nothing in your nature supplies for free. They learn that a request works better than a hint on somebody who does not read hints as instructions. Neither of you converts to the other's system. What changes over years is the translation speed: they stop hearing your vagueness as indifference, you stop hearing their precision as an accusation, and the same collision keeps happening with most of the injury taken out.

You tend to know how they are before they have decided to tell you. Your Neptune trines their Moon, so your imagination and their feelings run on compatible settings, with no translation step in between. They do not have to explain a mood. You do not have to be told when to stop talking. From outside it looks like the two of you have known each other much longer than the calendar says. You are as relieved by that as they are. Around you they can be unformed, tired, sentimental, or briefly ridiculous without any of it being held against them. Around them your own vagueness stops being a problem to be managed. Long unstructured time together, the sort with no agenda and nothing accomplished, is usually where this contact does its best work, which is not something either of you could put on a calendar and justify. One fact keeps this in proportion. Neptune stays in a single sign for well over a decade, so a whole span of people born near you will meet their Moon at roughly this angle. What the trine describes is the quality of the exchange, not its rarity, and the closeness the two of you have made out of it is your own doing rather than the geometry's. What it costs them is that feeling with somebody can substitute for doing anything about them. You are so well tuned to their state that you experience the response as already given. You felt it fully; something in you counts that as having answered. Meanwhile the practical thing goes undone, and because you are so obviously attentive, they are unlikely to say so. There is a second version that is quieter and worse: your sympathy softens their bad news to you. Their difficulty arrives already gentled, so a situation that should worry you does not, and you can be the closest person to somebody and the last to notice they are in real trouble. Your own cost is porousness without a brake. Their weather becomes yours automatically, and you have no natural resistance to it here, so you may spend days carrying a mood that belonged to their week and not yours. Ease is why it goes unnoticed. Nothing hurts, so nothing prompts a check. Make the softness do some work now and then. Ask a flat question about their circumstances and listen to the answer as fact rather than atmosphere. Do the specific thing while you are moved, before the feeling has time to stand in for it. The attunement is not fragile and it will not be damaged by being made useful.

One of you has needs with names, and it is not going to be you. Your Neptune faces their Moon across the whole width of the comparison. They arrive with an appetite that can be stated: company on Sunday, an answer by Friday, a routine that does not move. You arrive with something that has no shape and asks for nothing in particular. The two of you look at each other from opposite ends of that difference, and the difference organizes almost everything that happens between you. Roles form quickly and they harden. Their appetite becomes the visible one. You become the one who is fine, or elusive, or above it, depending on how charitable the day is. The trouble with being the one who apparently needs nothing is that ordinary appetite starts to look excessive by comparison. Their perfectly normal request for a plan sits next to your apparent needlessness and reads as demanding. They may begin apologizing for wanting things, or asking for less than they want, or asking somebody else instead. None of that was your intention and all of it followed from the arrangement. There is a second casting available, and pairs with this contact often try both. You become the rescuer, they become the one who is always in some difficulty, and the bond runs on that current for as long as the difficulty lasts. It is warm while it works and it puts them in a corner. Getting better means becoming less interesting to you, which is a poor thing to make anyone choose. Your own bill is the one you will not notice. Standing across from a person with clear needs is a comfortable way of never stating your own, and an unstated need does not go away, it goes underground and comes out as mood. You may find that you resent something you never asked for. Being the undemanding one is also a way of keeping the exits clear, and some part of you knows that, even while the arrangement is described as generosity. An axis supplies as much as it splits. They hold the knowledge that a want with a shape can actually be satisfied, which your side of the axis has never quite believed. You hold the knowledge that not every feeling requires a solution, that some of them are weather and should be allowed to pass through. Each of you is genuinely short of what the other has, and the exchange is available whenever either of you names the terms. Say one thing you need, in a plain sentence, on an ordinary day. That single move does more to unstick this than any amount of understanding on your part.

Everything they say to you arrives carrying a second meaning, and you are the one who put it there. Your Neptune sits on their Mercury, so your imagination occupies the same ground as their thinking and talking. A remark about the weather comes to you as a mood. A plain report of what happened comes to you as a story with a theme in it. You are not adding this deliberately. It happens between their sentence leaving them and your understanding of it arriving. Some of what this produces is genuinely rare. You can hear the idea they have not managed to finish. They start describing something badly, and you catch the shape underneath the bad description, and give it back in a form they can use. People almost never get that. Most listeners work with the words supplied. You work with what the words were reaching for, and for anyone whose thinking runs ahead of their vocabulary, this is the most useful audience they will find. Now the cost, which lands on them and is easy to miss. They cannot be taken literally by you. Say a modest thing and it comes back enlarged. Offer a passing thought and hear it quoted later as a conviction. They end up credited with a depth they did not intend, and the credit puts them in an awkward spot: accept it and live under a reputation for wisdom they have to keep supplying, or correct you and appear smaller than the version you were carrying. Most people take the first option, which means you are slowly being talked to by someone performing the person you described. The practical failure is narrower and more damaging. When they state a limit plainly, you may receive it as a mood that will pass. They say they cannot do the thing, or do not want to, and you hear reluctance rather than an answer, and go on as though the matter is open. That is not their evasion. Nobody here is being misled. It is the same softening that makes you a good listener working against the one kind of sentence that needs to arrive intact. Your own exposure is that you make plans with a version of what was said. Weeks later the two accounts of one conversation will not match, and both of you will be honestly certain. Something worth having grows out of this if you keep checking. Repeat their sentence back in their own words, not your improved ones, and let them confirm or fix it. Ask whether that was a decision or a thought. The habit costs you very little and it protects the part of the exchange that is actually valuable, which is your ability to hear what somebody means before they have found the language for it.

They think out loud badly, and you happen to hear it well. Your Neptune makes an easy angle to their Mercury, so their half-formed thinking has a place to land in your imagination without either of you working for it. As with any soft angle, it sits there unused until somebody decides to use it. The use is specific. They bring you something unresolved, a problem or a piece of work with no shape yet, and you do not try to solve it. You hold it, and it comes back with more in it than they brought. A conversation here can leave them further along without a single fact having changed hands, which is a strange result and a real one. If they make anything, you are unusually good company at the draft stage, when the thing is still too weak to defend. What they do for you is the reverse and equally useful. Your impressions are often accurate and almost never sayable. Their business is putting things into words, and around them you find yourself producing actual sentences about matters you normally carry as atmosphere. Once a thing has been said properly you can examine it, and some of it turns out to be true and some of it turns out to be a mood you have been treating as a conviction. That sorting is a service. The cost at this angle is mild. Because you soften what you hear, you may soften what you repeat, and your version of their remark can leave their meeting or their argument sounding kinder than it was. They may not know you are doing it. Somebody who relies on you to relay things will occasionally get a report with the edges filed off. It is not a large problem and it is worth knowing about. Left alone, all of this stays potential. Plenty of people hold this contact and never do more with it than find each other pleasant to talk to on a long drive. Nothing goes wrong. Nothing much happens either, and neither of you registers an absence, because you cannot miss a conversation you never had. What turns it on is bringing them the thing that is not ready, and asking them to say the plain version of something you have only ever felt. Both moves are small, both are slightly uncomfortable, and either one done regularly changes what the two of you are to each other.

They gave you an answer. You came away with an impression. Your Neptune squares their Mercury, so the part of you that dissolves outlines runs across the part of them that sorts, states, and keeps the record. What they said and what you received are related, and they are not the same document. This wears on them in a way that is hard to complain about. They are being precise and still not quite believed. The number gets remembered approximately. The condition attached to the yes drops off in transit. They find themselves repeating things to you that they know they said clearly the first time, and repetition starts to feel like being doubted. Worse is what happens when they insist. Push for exactness with you and they come across as cold, pedantic, or unwilling to enter the spirit of the thing, so the price of being accurate around you is looking like a smaller person. Some of them stop paying it and start agreeing vaguely, which suits nobody. Set aside the word this contact usually attracts. Nothing in either chart makes anyone a liar. What is actually going on is two different instruments for recording the same event: theirs keeps the sentence and the time, yours keeps the meaning and the feeling in the room. Both are honest and they do not reconcile on their own, and the gap between them is where the trouble lives. Your side of it is not comfortable either. Around them your certainty gets thin. A fact you were sure of turns out to be an atmosphere you had been carrying since a conversation you cannot reconstruct, and having that shown to you repeatedly is tiring, however gently it is done. You may also find you act on the version you received rather than the one that was given, and then have to account for the difference in front of somebody who has the original. There is genuine traction here, which is what a square is for. You are the person who will not accept a precise statement as a complete one, and they use precision that way more than they know, particularly when a subject is uncomfortable and an exact definition offers somewhere to stand. That question of yours is worth being asked. Meanwhile their exactness gives your perceptions something to test themselves against, and untested perceptions drift. What helps is smaller than a solution. When a thing has a date or a figure attached, let their record be the record, not because they are the more reliable person but because that is what their instrument is built to hold. When the question is what a situation actually amounts to, ask them to sit with it before filing it. Neither instrument is going to be retired here. What improves is the handling: you stop asking them to have meant more than they said, they stop asking you to prove what you noticed, and the same old difference starts producing better questions than either of you would have arrived at alone.

Their voice does something to you that their sentences do not account for. Your Neptune trines their Mercury, so whatever they say slides into your imagination without friction and comes to rest somewhere larger than where it started. Talking to them is restful in a way you would find difficult to describe to a third person. Nothing has to be spelled out. Nothing needs defending. For them the pleasure is being received completely. Most listeners are waiting to reply, or checking the argument, or quietly grading the delivery. You do none of that. You take the whole of what they are saying, including the tone and the hesitation, and they can feel that it landed. People tell you things at this angle that they have never tried to say to anybody, mostly because you did not make them justify the first sentence. Here is the seam. Being understood easily and being understood correctly feel identical from inside, and this contact removes every signal that would tell the two apart. You assume you got it. They assume you got it. Neither of you checks, and a misunderstanding can sit between you for a year quietly collecting detail. The eventual argument tends to skip the original subject entirely. What stings is the stretch of time you both spent agreeing about nothing. Your charity is part of the mechanism. Their weak idea gets a generous reading from you, and a generous reading from someone attentive is exactly what a weak idea needs to survive longer than it should. You are not flattering them. You genuinely hear the best possible version, and the best possible version is what you reflect back. Somebody who brings you their plans regularly may end up with better plans than they deserve in your account and worse ones in the world. The everyday casualty is the boring specific: the amount, the date, who was going to do which part. Pinning that down feels almost rude between two people who understand each other, and it is not rude. The pair who keep the dull details in writing keep the good part of this intact. The habit to build is asking for the ugly version. What is the part of this you would not say to someone sympathetic. What did they actually reply, in their words. You will not lose the ease by doing that, because the ease was never conditional on being vague. It was there before either of you started talking.

Between the two of you there is always a document and always a feeling, and you are never the one holding the document. Your Neptune faces their Mercury. What they bring is the sequence: what was said, in what order, by whom, and what follows from it. What you bring is everything the sequence left out, which is usually the part you consider the point. Your evidence does not survive translation into their format, and their format is the one the argument always runs in. From where they stand, this can be a slow erosion of confidence in their own reporting. They tell you exactly what happened and watch it get received as one possible reading. Do that often enough and a careful person starts to wonder whether accuracy is worth the trouble, since it never seems to settle anything with you. There is a particular sting in being told, by implication, that the true version missed the meaning. Some people respond by going quiet about details altogether, and that is a loss, because the details were the one thing being reliably supplied. What it does to you is a standing doubt you cannot argue with. Their questions are reasonable and you have no answer in their format. You know something about the situation and cannot produce the evidence, and after the third time you may stop trying, or start believing that what you know does not count. It does count. It is simply not admissible in the form they are asking for, and the two of you would do better arguing about that than about the facts of the evening. This axis also produces drift. A conversation starts with a subject and a shape, and somewhere in the middle the shape goes, and neither of you can find the way back to what was being decided. You will not be sure at the end whether anything was agreed. That is the geometry, not carelessness on either side. The standoff is also a supply line. What they hold is a record that will still be there next year, checkable by anybody, indifferent to how the room felt at the time. What you hold is the ability to tell when a correct account has left out the thing that actually mattered. Each of you is permanently short of the other's equipment, and no amount of arguing is going to merge the two into one. What tends to change, over years, is not the disagreement but your regard for it. You stop treating their exactness as a failure of feeling. They stop treating your impressions as a refusal to be pinned down. Two people who can do that get a fuller view of anything they both look at than either could assemble alone.
